body:
Additional feedback on v20-IoT.

The definition of L1/L2/L3 does not fit well with v20. It is linked to applications and v20 is about devices.

    Level 1 is meant for all software -- now ¿all devices?
    Level 2 is for applications that contain sensitive data, which requires protection. -- most IoT devices can be consider as containing sensitive data, at least, personal data of the owner of the device.
    Level 3 is for the most critical applications -- now how we define a critical device? I guess not only for its purpose but also for where the IoT device is place.

v20.1 & v20.4 could be only one requirment: Verify that debug interfaces (USB, JTAG...) are disabled or have appropiate protections against unauthorized access.
v20.6 could be splitted on two requirements. Require that sensitive data is not stored unencrypted on the device for L3 seems not enough. Hardware based protection should be added for that Level (Secure Elements, TPMs...maybe also TEEs).
v20.8 & v20.11 could be only one requirement: Verify that any sensitive data is sent over a secure channel (encryption+integrity). No matter how and by whom.
v20.13 based on how L2 is defined for IoT/embedded devices...this requirement could be complicate to accomplish, expensive for some type of IoT devices.
v20.15 same as above.
v20.17 only the boot image? This requirement is related to secure boot mechanisms which in most cases involves more than the verification of the boot image. At least, firmware image should be also verify. The need of a device's unique key (usually OTP protected) stored at manufacturing time should be mandatory for a good secure boot implementation.
v20.24 maybe also fault injection resistance.
v20.27 maybe also for L2
v20.29 some alternatives for isolation between apps could be TEEs (Intel SGX, ARM Trustzone based...) or hypervisors. Is this what you mean by kernel containers?

I agree on ossie-git last comment. IoT section is different from Web Applications and Mobile Applications ones. It seems better to create something new. One example is my first suggestion related to L1/2/3 definition, for IoT should be new or slightly modified.
